correctness.rationale: For named parameters, homogeneity identifies complete nonalgebraic singleton types with realizable induced one-point extensions. Their below and above sets are respectively an ideal and a filter, with every below point strictly below every above point. If both are nonempty they must use just one component. The five ideals give I=1+2z+z²+z³, filters give its reversal J, and the three mixed extensions have degrees 2,2,3. This gives I^k+J^k−1+k(2z²+z³). Exact independent checks covered all 15,657 interior log-concavity inequalities through k=102 and reproduced the strict valley c153>c154=c155<c156 at k=103, with difference 2495932549114782218173979671914572799723401947915153095744250035552. All coefficients are positive, so log-concavity implies unimodality through 102. For general Q, the two normalized power-polynomial profiles are reflected laws of independent ideal sizes: noncentral mean puts positive mass in separated linear-size windows, and Hoeffding makes the midpoint exponentially smaller than at least one coefficient in each window. The mixed correction vanishes above m. For V, mean 7/5 and variance 26/25 give more than half mass within k/20 of the mean for k≥10000; the two midpoint tails are bounded by 2 exp(−k/500) using distance k/10−1 and range 3, which is less than 1/(k/5+4).
residual_risks: The frozen narrative overstates check_independent.py: its loop asserts unimodality, not log-concavity. The latter is checked by check.py and by the new exact reproductions, so this does not affect the theorem.
No complete classification of 104≤k<10000 is asserted.

value.rationale: The grading is intrinsic to the extension problem and disjoint copies of the smallest asymmetric fork give a canonical family. The surprisingly delayed first valley is an exact obstruction to inferring shape from the individual one-sided counts. The general mean criterion explains a mechanism that other repeated component families can use, beyond the finite census.
residual_risks: The mean criterion is sufficient, not a classification at the symmetric mean.
